items.title: Son of Cuban singer Haila María Mompié arrested on armed robbery, drug charges, Miami police say
items.text:
Haned Mota Mompié, 25, a Cuban songwriter and the son of renowned Cuban singer Haila María Mompié, was arrested Wednesday in Miami, according to Miami Police Department arrest reports.

MIAMI — Haned Mota Mompié, 25, a songwriter and the son of renowned Cuban singer Haila María Mompié , was arrested Wednesday in Miami, according to Miami Police Department arrest reports. Leer en español Jail records show he is facing charges of attempted armed robbery with a weapon, possession of crack cocaine and possession of methamphetamine. According to police, the attempted robbery occurred shortly after midnight Nov. 25 at a store inside Miami Plaza Tower, located at 1500 NE Miami Place. Police said a store clerk told officers that Mota Mompié entered the business with a white shirt covering his face and approached him while armed with a curved pocketknife. They said he allegedly demanded that the clerk hand over all the money. The clerk stepped back and began calling 911, prompting Mota Mompié to reach over the counter and attempt to open the cash register, according to the arrest report. However, police said he was unsuccessful and left the store after the clerk told him security was on the property. The clerk followed him outside and saw him remove the shirt covering his face, police said. Investigators said they reviewed surveillance footage that captured the entire incident. The video showed a man wearing a white shirt over his head, a black shirt featuring a cat design and black pants. The footage also showed him carrying a curved pocketknife, according to police. Officers later spotted a man matching the suspect’s description near Northwest Second Avenue and 12th Street. Police said Mota Mompié, was wearing the same distinctive black shirt seen in the surveillance footage. When officers attempted to detain him, he fled on foot southbound along Northwest Second Avenue, the report states. Police said he was eventually apprehended near the 200 block of Northwest 11th Terrace. Police said a search following his arrest turned up the pocketknife allegedly used in the attempted robbery. Investigators subsequently conducted a show-up identification, during which the store clerk identified Mota Mompié as the person who had attempted to rob him, according to the report. Police also said Mota Mompié was transported to MPD’s robbery office, where he was advised of his constitutional rights. After waiving those rights, he provided a recorded statement and confessed to the robbery, according to investigators. A second arrest report details additional drug allegations stemming from a search conducted after Mota Mompié was taken into custody. According to that report, officers recovered a small pink bag containing a white, rock-like substance suspected to be crystal methamphetamine from his front left jeans pocket. Police said at least four small yellow bags containing a white, powder-like substance suspected to be crack cocaine were allegedly found in his rear right pocket, along with a red blade. The substances were identified as suspected narcotics based on their appearance, consistency and packaging, according to the report. As of Friday afternoon, Mota Mompié was being held without bond at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center.

items.title: More than a decade in the works, Hilton Miami Beach set to open in 2027
items.text:
Find out the Hilton’s plans and what you can expect at the hotel.

After years of construction delays , fires, financial challenges and legal disputes, a group of historic buildings in Miami Beach is set to open as a new hotel.
The Hilton Miami Beach, on 2000 Park Ave. in the Museum Historic District, will open in early 2027. Guests can now make reservations at the planned 289-room hotel for March 1, 2027, and beyond, according to its website.
Owned by the Chetrit Group, the Lotus Group and the Jesta Group, owner of the Clevelander on Ocean Drive, the new accommodation comprises buildings spanning a city block that have been empty for years, including the iconic Collins Park Hotel.
The Hilton Miami Beach, walking distance to the Miami Beach Convention Center, will have three swimming pools, a workout room, high speed Wi-Fi in each guest room, and other modern amenities. It’ll do so while bringing together several buildings that date back to 1938 and 1953.
Collins Park Hotel, designed by Art Deco expert, architect Henry Hohauser and finished in 1939, has a curved glass entrance pavilion and rounded corners. During World War II, it served as military housing for the U.S. Army Air Forces Technical Training Command.
The Adams Hotel, designed by L. Murray Dixon in 1938, has a stepped tower, ribbon windows and a futuristic rooftop lantern.
Others are the Tyler Hotel, an Albert Annis creation in 1940, Copley Terrace Apartments, S&M Apartments, later known as Sunking II, and Lord Charles and Gamshire buildings.
The Hilton Miami Beach said in a statement that the various buildings will showcase Miami Beach’s architectural evolution from Streamline Moderne to postwar Miami Modern design, known as MiMo. They’ll preserve “the architectural character of the original structures” and celebrate the history behind them, the company said.
The hotel’s interiors will feature palettes of soft pinks and greens, polished metals, rounded form and geometric patterns, reminiscent of Miami Beach’s art deco and mid-century architecture
“Few hotels offer guests the opportunity to experience nearly 90 years of architectural history in one property,” said Bruce Siegel, vice president of operations and general manager of Hilton Miami Beach, in a statement. “We’ve preserved the architectural details that make these structures unique while introducing a new place to dine, connect and gather whether traveling for business or leisure.”
The project is over a decade in the making, but preservationists see it as one that respects the history of the area.
“They are bringing back the facades,” and “the interiors will have Art Deco features,” Daniel Ciraldo, former director of the Miami Design Preservation League, said in an interview with the Miami Herald. “They’re bringing it back to life and that’s what we need here.”
The buildings have had brushes with death. In 2007, the buildings caught fire. In 2011, the Copley Terrace Apartments, already empty, suffered another fire.
The Chetrit Group bought the buildings in 2012. Construction started in 2015 but subsequently faced various hurdles.
In 2018, a construction worker died on the site of the Collins Park Hotel. The U.S. Department of Labor and OSHA investigated, fined and cited the general contractors including the Rinaldi Group for several workplace safety violations. items.title: Nearly $9M in taxes returned to Miami-Dade County Public Schools
items.text:
Miami-Dade County Public Schools is set to receive $8,995,000 in unused tax collector fees, money left after operating expenses, the tax collector said.

The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Miami-Dade County Public Schools is set to receive nearly $9 million in leftover money from the county’s tax collector.
The office of the tax collector announced Friday that it will return $8,995,000 in unused fees to the school district. Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said in a statement that the funds were left over after the office covered its operating expenses.
The money is available to the district to support students and teachers.
Under Florida law, any money left over after county tax collectors have covered their operating expenses must be distributed to government agencies that paid fees to the office.
